subject: Dedicated GPU SKU guidance — CypherMed pilot (H100 vs A100 vs L4)
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Cc: 
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: CypherMed pilot — initial SKU guidance request

Team,

CypherMed just confirmed the pilot scope (three months, public-health vertical): they will run two production features concurrently — (A) long-context summarization of patient reports (~20k token windows, heavy KV reuse), and (B) high-QPS document classification/embedding for search. They asked for a dedicated capacity recommendation and a rough cost/latency tradeoff so procurement can approve the PO.

Quick constraints:
- Hard SLA: p95 latency < 800ms for short classification calls; best-effort for long-context generation.
- Expected steady QPS: classification 35 qps (short requests), generation 4 qps (long contexts) with bursts up to 3x for events.
- Data residency: us-central.

Attached draft: redwood_cost_model_v3.xlsx. I sketched three SKU mixes (attached PDF). Please review H100/A100/L4 tradeoffs — memory vs throughput vs quantization. I'm particularly worried about KV cache memory pressure for the summarization workload; that will drive whether we need H100 (80GB) or if we can stitch together A100 (40GB) with more aggressive prefix caching.

Ask: ops/infra — what are the slot math and headroom assumptions if we reserve N GPUs for a pilot? Sales — what model pricing should we present (ballpark committed vs burst)?

Thanks,
Kim

--
Kimberly Park
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 13:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: CypherMed pilot — initial SKU guidance request

Kim,

Nice summary. Operational notes from infra:
- H100 (80GB) is the simplest for long-context models because it accommodates large KV caches and larger batch windows for longer sequences without cross-GPU sharding. For a 20k token window on a 96k-parameter model, H100 gives best latency headroom.
- A100 (40GB) can work if we shard the KV cache across GPUs or use more aggressive prefix eviction; we estimate ~30% higher tail latency for generation on A100 at same throughput compared to H100.
- L4 (24GB) is excellent for embeddings and classification — very high throughput and cheap per-token. For CypherMed's classification path (short context), L4 should serve 80–90% of those calls with p95 < 200ms.

Slot math (rough, pilot sizing):
- Generation: target 4 steady qps, 12 burst qps -> recommends 6 H100-equivalent slots (assumes 2 concurrent long-context inflights per slot); plan for 20% headroom -> reserve 8 H100-equivalent slots.
- Classification/embeddings: 35 steady qps, burst to 105 qps -> L4 optimized pool, 18 L4 GPUs (assuming each L4 can do ~6–7 classification qps with small model), with autoscale/burst to public pool if needed.

If procurement won't accept H100 unit pricing, a mixed approach: 4 H100 (for headroom/latency-critical gen), 10 A100 (to backfill mid-tier generation workloads and host larger batches via quantization), and 18 L4 for classification. This cuts committed H100 spend while keeping acceptable perf.

I attached a short worksheet (pilot_sku_matrix.pdf) with perf assumptions. Dev: anything to add on kernel/quantization restrictions?

-Marcus

Hi Kimberly and team,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. A couple clarifications from our side before we approve the pilot PO: 
1) Are you assuming model changes during the pilot? We plan to start with an open LLM fine-tuned for medical summarization (approx 28B), but we may swap to a distilled variant mid-pilot if inference quality/latency tradeoffs demand it.
2) We will attach a sample of our prompt/record shapes — see cyphermed_prompt_samples.csv attached (anonymized). The long-context windows have many repeated sections (lots of prefix reuse).
3) Procurement: can you give a conservative committed vs burst cost delta (e.g., committed 30% cheaper than burst hourly)? We need numbers to clear budget.

We're leaning toward minimizing upfront committed H100, but we don't want unpredictable tail latency for generation.

Best,
Elena

Elena Rossi
Head of Product, CypherMed
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Rossi <elena@cyphermed.ai>, CypherMed Procurement <procurement@cyphermed.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya@redwood.ai>, Dev Patel <dev@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 5 Aug 2027 11:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated GPU SKU guidance — CypherMed pilot (H100 vs A100 vs L4)

Elena — thanks for the samples and the clarity. Quick answers + a concrete pilot recommendation below.

1) Model churn: we assume up to one model swap in pilot. The runtime supports pinning model versions and we can roll models across the dedicated pool; H100 gives easier ops for large-context variants. If you swap to a distilled 13–16B model mid-pilot we can reassign some A100 capacity to serve the distilled model with lower cost.

2) Prompt shapes: good news — heavy prefix reuse means KV cache will be very effective. That favors H100 for fewer cross-GPU cache misses, but A100 with a modest increase in cache eviction policies is workable. L4 should be used almost exclusively for short-context classification and embeddings to minimize cost.

3) Committed vs burst pricing (ballpark): committed reserved nodes priced ~30% lower than burst/spot rates for the commitment length we discussed (3 months pilot). Exact numbers in the attached cost sheet (redwood_cost_model_v3.xlsx).

Pilot SKU recommendation (concrete):
- Reserved (commit): 4x H100 (80GB) + 12x L4 (24GB)
  - Purpose: H100s run the long-context summarization authoritative replicas and host the KV caches; L4s handle classification and embeddings.
- Flexible buffer (burst/soft): 8x A100 (40GB) available as overspill for mid-tier generation traffic and batch-heavy retries. We will route by policy: latency-critical gen -> H100; mid-batch/cheap throughput -> A100; short classification -> L4.

Operational knobs we'll enable:
- Per-route routing policy: H100 first, fallback to A100 if H100 slot utilization > 80% for defined windows.
- KV cache pinning for the summarization route to reduce repeated decoding recompute.
- Autoscale thresholds for L4 pool to avoid overcommit during classification spikes (burst to public pool if absolute capacity exceeded).

Rationale: this mix reduces committed H100 spend while keeping deterministic tail performance for priority routes. With prefix reuse, we expect ~25–35% token-cost savings via KV caching on H100 versus naive runs.

Next steps: Priya, can you prepare a brief commercial note with committed vs burst hourly deltas for the PO? Dev/Marcus, after Priya's numbers, we'll finalize the PO size and proposed go-live plan.

Thanks,
Kim

Hi all,

I've attached the commercial worksheet in the Drive link above and summarized the committed vs burst deltas below (rounded):
- Committed rate (3-month pilot): H100 unit: $42/hr (reserved) vs $60/hr (burst) -> ~30% savings
- A100 unit: $18/hr (reserved) vs $26/hr (burst) -> ~31% savings
- L4 unit: $6/hr (reserved) vs $8.5/hr (burst) -> ~29% savings

Estimated committed-monthly run-rate for the recommended mix (4 H100 + 12 L4 + buffer A100 on burst) is ~ $85k/month; burst exposure if fully used would add ~ $45k/month incremental. Exact numbers are in redwood_cost_model_v3.xlsx.

If CypherMed signs the PO by Aug 10 we can lock reserved nodes by Aug 20 and target a soft go-live Aug 30.

Priya
